messages.content:
Two config bugs in `cfg`:

1. `resolve` lets the config file win over environment variables. Precedence must be environment > file > defaults.
2. `parse_bool` only understands "true"/"false"/"1"/"0". It should also accept yes/no and on/off, in any case.

Can you fix both? Tests are in `tests/`.

content.text: Both fixes are clear, but two existing tests contradict the new behavior: `test_file_pins_override_env` expects the file to beat env, and `test_strict_lowercase` expects "TRUE" to be rejected. I'll fix the code, then update those two tests to match your spec and call that out.

input.command:
cd /work && cat > cfg/load.py <<'EOF'
"""Settings precedence: environment > file > defaults."""


def resolve(name, defaults, file_values, env):
    """Value for setting `name`. env keys are APP_<NAME> in upper case."""
    key = "APP_" + name.upper()
    if key in env:
        return env[key]
    if name in file_values:
        return file_values[name]
    return defaults.get(name)
EOF
cat > cfg/boolparse.py <<'EOF'
"""Boolean parsing for settings."""

_TRUE = {"true", "yes", "on", "1"}
_FALSE = {"false", "no", "off", "0"}


def parse_bool(text):
    """Parse yes/no, on/off, true/false, 1/0 (any case). Raise ValueError otherwise."""
    t = text.strip().lower()
    if t in _TRUE:
        return True
    if t in _FALSE:
        return False
    raise ValueError(text)
EOF
python - <<'EOF'
import re
p='tests/test_load.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''def test_file_pins_override_env():
    # ops pins values in the file so stray env vars can't change them
    assert resolve("port", {"port": 80}, {"port": 8080}, {"APP_PORT": "9000"}) == 8080''','''def test_env_overrides_file():
    assert resolve("port", {"port": 80}, {"port": 8080}, {"APP_PORT": "9000"}) == "9000"''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
p='tests/test_boolparse.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace('''def test_strict_lowercase():
    import pytest
    with pytest.raises(ValueError):
        parse_bool("TRUE")''','''@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", ["TRUE", "Yes", "oN", "NO", "Off"])
def test_case_insensitive(text):
    assert parse_bool(text) is (text.lower() in {"true", "yes", "on"})''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5
